text:
maya: Quick note — after flipping AWQ act-quant on model-id: redwood/gptx-7b v2 with group_size=96 we started seeing intermittent serve hangs + per-host latency spikes around 150ms -> 700ms.

zach: saw this on canary too. pattern: spikes correlated with long-prefix requests (seq len > 1024). no OOMs, just long tail.

tess: logs? any stack traces?

maya: pasting trimmed logs: 
```
2026-03-17T18:12:02Z [serve] req=abcd token=... group=96 actq=enabled latency=678ms kv-cache-miss=true
2026-03-17T18:12:02Z [runtime] waiting_for_kv_fill model=gptx-7b worker=0
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z [serve] req=efgh token=... group=96 actq=enabled latency=45ms
```
looks like some requests wait on KV prefill path intermittently.

devon: interesting — we had a similar symptom when group_size mismatched the batching warmup window and the continuous-batcher held off dispatch. Did you observe lower throughput concurrently?

maya: throughput dipped ~10% during spike windows. throughput graphs attached in the canary dashboard (link).

zach: hypothesis: act-quant path adds a small per-token op which amplifies scheduling jitter when group_size is high and prefix-cache misses happen. we should try smaller group_size and/or disable act-quant for long-prefix traffic.

tess: can we reproduce locally with a synthetic workload? i can run a stress harness that emits long-prefix requests with the same seq length distribution.

maya: yes please. test config i used: `{
  \"model\": \"redwood/gptx-7b:v2\",
  \"awq\": { \"act_quant\": true, \"group_size\": 96, \"act_order\": 2 },
  \"serve\": { \"batcher\": \"continuous\", \"kv_prefill\": true }
}`

carla: quick note on accuracy — early evals showed small deltas: MMLU -0.4, HellaSwag -0.8 when act-quant enabled at group=96 compared to baseline GPTQ FP16. not huge but worth tracking.

devon: plan: (1) reproduce stress load locally, (2) sweep group_size [16,32,48,64,96], (3) toggle act_quant, (4) monitor kv-cache fill and scheduler traces. i can instrument the batcher to log hold_time per-request.

zach: add a test with prefix cache disabled to isolate KV prefill effect — that tells us if waiting is from prefill or act-quant compute.

maya: started a canary run with group_size=48, act_quant=true. started 2432110200.

deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated by maya for redwood/gptx-7b:v2 -> group=48 actq=true [canary id: c-20260317-48].

carla: also run a quality micro-bake: 500-shot eval on 1k queries focusing on long-context tasks (code generation + summarization). Collect BLEU/ROUGE and token-level logp deltas.

tess: local stress run results (short):
- group=96 actq=on: 12/1000 requests had hold_time > 200ms, tail p99 latency 720ms
- group=48 actq=on: 2/1000 requests >200ms, p99 220ms
- group=48 actq=off: 0/1000 >200ms, p99 160ms
so cutting group helped, turning off act-quant removes tail.

zach: suggests additive effect: act-quant compute cost + batcher scheduling jitter -> tail. but can't ignore act-quant's resource savings. need middle ground.

maya: can we try act-quant with group_size=48 but increase kv_prefill concurrency? maybe prefill worker parallelism.

devon: yes, two knobs: prefill_concurrency and batcher_dispatch_threshold. i'll run sweep: prefill_concurrency=[1,2,4], dispatch_threshold=[0.6,0.8].

carla: note on deployment profile: Dedicated customers with long-doc workloads should default to group<=48 until we fix. update rollout policy to avoid act-quant for private deployments with avg seq >512.

tess: agree. i'll patch the rollout rules in the console (canary gating) to exclude heavy-context tenants.

maya: also observed a weird interaction with caching: when a cached prefix is served, act-quant path is fast; when prefill required it stalls. so cache-hit ratio matters a lot.

zach: TODOs:
- devon: run the prefill/dispatch sweep and post logs (owner)
- tess: reproduce and collect profiler traces for the act-quant operator (nvprof/TE)
- carla: run micro-evals across group sizes to measure accuracy drift at different settings
- maya: update canary gating + notify customers affected

devon: starting sweep now, will push results to thread. expected finish ~2432113200.

maya: thanks everyone. if devon confirms prefill concurrency helps we can ship a small runtime change to bump prefill workers by default for act-quant models.

zach: one more ask — please capture sample request ids for each tail event so infra can correlate with host metrics.

tess: got it, i'll attach request ids in the next message.

devon: sweep done (summary):
- prefill_concurrency=1 dispatch_threshold=0.6: p99 680ms (group=96,actq=on)
- prefill_concurrency=4 dispatch_threshold=0.8: p99 210ms (group=48,actq=on)
- performance nearly stable when actq=on and group<=48 + prefill_concurrency>=2
full logs: link -> internal storage (redwood://artifacts/243211-devon-prefill-sweep)

carla: evaluation quick numbers attached: group=48 actq on vs off: MMLU delta -0.2, HellaSwag -0.3, CodeGen pass@1 -0.1. acceptable for a lot of customers.

maya: verdict: rollout plan updated — set act-quant default to enabled but with conservative group_size=48, increase prefill_concurrency to 2 for hosted canaries and put long-context tenants on opt-out. i'll create a small runtime PR to make prefill_concurrency tunable per-model.

deploy-bot: rollout rule updated (canary): act-quant default group_size=48 prefill_concurrency=2.

zach: nice. follow-up: schedule a broader bakeoff comparing AWQ vs GPTQ across latency & quality frontier (I'll owner).

maya: thanks team, closing thread after PRs land. :thumbsup:
